Rishi,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement checklist and upcoming security review we need a concise deliverable that covers:
- Current subprocessor roster and which subprocessors handle key material or encryption (who holds HSM/KMS keys)
- Network/data custody boundaries (what is stored in-region vs cross-border)
- Controls for KV cache, prefixes, and log retention tied to the DPA/TIA mapping
- Any UK IDTA/UK Addendum implications if we enable routing to gb-west region

Can you send a short checklist + supporting artifacts (matrix + control summary) by EOD PST? Our procurement review is Monday morning. If there are gaps we may need a brief call with engineering.

Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Kim (infrastructure ops) to confirm precise language for the DPA/TIA mapping. Quick notes up-front:

- Subprocessor roster: attached matrix (redwood-subprocessor-matrix.csv). It indicates which subprocessors have access to customer data and which hold KMS/HSM keys.
- Key custody: Redwood uses customer-separated KMS keys for Private deployments. For Hosted API, we manage keys in our cloud KMS; HSM-backed keys are used for Dedicated clusters on request (see controls summary).
- Data residency: default routing is region-specific; cross-border flows are flagged in the matrix and annotated with the applicable SCC/UK addendum implications.
- KV/prefix caching: caching is transient; KV cache persists in-memory on serving nodes and is not written to persistent storage unless explicitly enabled — documented in the controls summary.

Elaine — attaching a one-page MAP and short answers to your two clarifications. See attachments (MAP_HealthSys_v1.xlsx; redwood-security-controls-summary.pdf). Summary below:

1) Hosted BYOK: We support an integration that allows customers to bring keys (BYOK) via partner KMS connectors. HSM-backed BYOK in Hosted requires an onboarding security review and a scoped SLA amendment — owner: Jordan (sales); timeline: 3-4 weeks typical. Mitigation if BYOK is not enabled: envelope encryption with our KMS + customer-provided wrapping key; split-key available by request for high-sensitivity customers.

2) UK Addendum & route-to-gb-west: Routing to gb-west triggers the UK Addendum path for customers with UK-resident data. Technical changes: dedicated routing endpoint, optional dedicated cluster for residency, and explicit routing flags in the control plane. We will provide clause-level evidence (SCC+UK Addendum mapping) and a supplemental evidence pack if HealthSys signs the addendum. Owner: Marissa (legal) to confirm exact clause mapping; Owner: Kim (ops) to provide configuration steps.

Next steps (MAP, deadlines):
- Rishi: final MAP + evidence pack (EOD PST Friday)
- Kim: ops runbook for enabling dedicated routing and KMS onboarding (2 business days)
- Marissa: DPA/UK Addendum clause-level mapping (2 business days)
- Jordan: finalize BYOK contract language and SLA amendment (partner with procurement)

If that schedule works I will upload the full evidence pack to the secure drive and trigger a short sync for Monday at 9am PST.

Attachments: MAP_HealthSys_v1.xlsx; redwood-security-controls-summary.pdf; redwood-subprocessor-matrix.csv; docusign_dpa_link.txt
